# Coding agent packs

**Generated by `python coding-agents/compile.py`. Do not hand-edit.**

Sources of truth: [`../variants/`](../variants/) (one directory per skill) and
[`../profiles/`](../profiles/) (where each agent reads instructions from).

## Variants

| Variant | What it governs |
|---|---|
| `unified` | Recommended default. One agent, both jobs — developer chat and documents. |
| `qt6-cmake-cpp` | Workload skill for Qt 6 desktop applications in C++ built with CMake — new projects, UI redesigns of existing Qt Widgets apps, GUIs that drive a command-line engine through QProcess, offscreen GUI test harnesses, CI o… |
| `universal-agent-context` | Always-on process layer for any coding-agent session in one of this owner's Git repositories (Arena Agent Mode, Claude Code, or a comparable harness). |

## Rules of thumb

- **Load at most one output register** (`unified`): it decides how the visible answer reads and which of several acceptable solutions to prefer.
- **Load the process layer every session** (`universal-agent-context`): it decides what must exist and be verified before "done" may be said. It is installed as a skill directory, never inlined — its guide is hash-pinned.
- **Load a workload skill only when the repository matches it** (`qt6-cmake-cpp`); each description says when to skip it.
- Precedence when texts collide: owner instruction → repository evidence → process layer → workload skill → register.
- Every agent reads `AGENTS.md` except Cursor (prefers `.mdc`) — if you want
  one loader paragraph to work everywhere, start there.
- `.agents/skills/<name>/` is read natively by Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and
  Copilot; `.claude/skills/` by Claude Code, OpenCode and Copilot; `.qwen/skills/` by
  Qwen Code. One checked-in skill directory plus two copies covers every harness here
  that has a skill surface.

See [`../philosophy/conflicts.md`](../philosophy/conflicts.md) for why the three
philosophies are kept apart, how `unified` resolves them, and how the register
composes with the process layer.
